title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes build Grothendieck's 'Teichmüller groupoid' by choosing base points near the boundary of moduli space. G is a stable graph of a degenerate curve: vertices are components, edges are nodes. G has one distinguished vertex s0 whose component Y is a P^1 with four special points I, i.e. a four-holed sphere. Every other vertex is a pair of pants. So G indexes a one-dimensional boundary stratum isomorphic to M_{0,I} = M_{0,4}.

The objects.
- SP_G is a set (later a bundle over the stratum) of base-point data attached to G.
- U is a structure group, most plausibly U(1). Each T_i is the U-torsor of real tangent directions at the special point i of Y.
- A is the set of edges, split as A1 ⊔ A2. A1 is the set of edges not incident to s0 (the data T_{A1}, already handled on the previous page). A2 = A \ A1 is the set of edges incident to s0.
- J is the set of oriented half-edges at s0, so |J| = 4 and J corresponds to I.

Splitting J. The previous page splits J = J_I ⊔ J_II ⊔ J_III.
- J_I: half-edges whose other end lies at another vertex. They contribute T_{J_I}^Y = ∏_{i∈J_I} T_i.
- J_II: loops at s0. Their two half-edges are exchanged by a fixed-point-free involution σ. They contribute T_{J_II}^Y = ∏_{α∈J_II/σ} (T_i ∧ T_j), the contracted product over U of the two direction torsors at the ends of the loop. The underbraces say there are 0, 1 or 2 loops, with 2 factors in each wedge.
- J_III: half-edges with a degree-2 structure. Most likely these are edges whose far end has an extra ±1 ambiguity, e.g. through a symmetric component. They contribute ∏_{i∈J_III} T_i ∧_{±1} J̃_{III,i}, a U-torsor obtained by twisting T_i by a {±1}-torsor.

Why contracted products. This is the familiar picture of node smoothing. The smoothing parameter of a node lives in T_p ⊗ T_q, so its argument lives in the U-torsor T_p ∧ T_q.

Globalising. As Y varies, these products become U^{J_I}-, U^{J_II/σ}- and U^{J_III}-torsors T_I, T_II, T_III over M_{0,I}. Their fibre product is T_{A2}, a U^{A2}-torsor, since A2 ≅ J_I ⊔ (J_II/σ) ⊔ J_III. Hence SP_G ≅ T_{Â1} × T_{Â2}: a constant U^{Â1}-torsor times a U^{A2}-torsor over M_{0,I}. Concretely, SP_G is the torus bundle of 'angular/twist' data over the stratum, i.e. the real-oriented-blow-up boundary.

The programme. Grothendieck next wants to describe the action of the fundamental groupoid of the Teichmüller object T_G on SP_G, using well-chosen base points. He picks the Y lying over the 5 ramification points of M_{0,I} → M_{0,I}/S_4. These are the 4-pointed lines with automorphism group larger than the Klein group (order > 4, in fact 8 or 12).
- Three of them correspond to the three partitions of type (2,2) of I, equivalently the three cyclic ('circle') structures on I. These are the 'square' configurations, cross-ratio −1, 2, 1/2, with dihedral automorphism group of order 8.
- Two are equianharmonic, cross-ratio e^{±iπ/3}, with tetrahedral group A4 of order 12.

The next page treats the circle case. Rotations act simply transitively on I, which identifies all the T_i, and gives T_i ≅ H ×_{±1} ω_Q for an orientation ω_Q of the circle.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The count of 5 special points and the automorphism orders (8 and 12, both multiples of 4 and > 4) are correct for M_{0,4} → M_{0,4}/S_4: 3 points over j=1728 and 2 over j=0.

Minor notational inconsistency: the page writes T_{A_2} in the text and T_{Â_2} in the displayed formula, and labels the latter a U^{A_2}-torsor. The hat seems to mark a set of oriented or extended edges; its meaning is not fixed on this page.
The precise meaning of J_III and of the {±1}-torsor J̃_{III,i} cannot be fully determined from this page alone. The previous page says only that J_III carries a degree-2 map.

ideas.what: Base-point data near a boundary stratum. These are torsors under a torus U^{edges}, built from contracted products T_p ∧ T_q of tangent-direction torsors at the two branches of each node.
ideas.modern_name: Real oriented blow-up of the Deligne–Mumford boundary; tangential base points; twist/gluing angles (Fenchel–Nielsen twist torus).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (smoothing parameter in T_p⊗T_q); Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov and Looijenga for the oriented blow-up (1990s); Deligne/Ihara for tangential base points.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses base points at infinity for the Teichmüller tower only qualitatively.

ideas.what: Case split of the half-edges at the 4-valent vertex: ordinary edges, loops (paired by an involution) and edges with a ±1 twist. The torsor over the stratum is factored accordingly.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of the boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n} indexed by a stable graph with one 4-valent vertex.

ideas.what: Base points for the Teichmüller groupoid placed at the orbifold points of M_{0,4}/S_4: the 3 square (D4) points tied to the type (2,2) partitions and circle structures, and the 2 equianharmonic (A4) points. These replace or complement base points at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Base points at elliptic or orbifold points; finite-subgroup (torsion) generation of mapping class groups.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold base points in the modular-tower literature (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) are used mostly at infinity. Base points at torsion points are related to the Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 presentation of SL2(Z).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions dimension-1 modular levels (M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}) as generating; it is unclear whether elliptic points are used as base points there.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an action of the fundamental groupoid of the Teichmüller stratum T_G on the torus bundle SP_G, using as base points the symmetric 4-pointed lines (square and equianharmonic) rather than only tangential base points at infinity. The equivariance under the finite groups G_Y (orders 8 and 12) is meant to rigidify the choice. This variant of the Teichmüller groupoid, with base points at orbifold points of the dimension-1 strata, does not seem developed in the literature, which favours maximally degenerate tangential base points.
missed.quote: On va s'intéresser à des "pts bases" bien choisis ... aux 5 pts de ramification pour M_{0,I} ... pour l'action des groupes finis G_Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Symmetric base points could give a GT- or Teichmüller-groupoid presentation in which some relations come from finite automorphism groups (orders 4 and 6 torsion) rather than from braiding at infinity. This might simplify the 'two-level' generation statements, but its value is speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is a routine factorisation of the node-smoothing torus bundle over a dimension-1 boundary stratum. The mildly unusual element is the plan to place base points of the Teichmüller groupoid at the orbifold points of M_{0,4} with automorphism groups of order 8 and 12. That is a less common choice than tangential base points at infinity, but it is only begun here.
transcription_corrections: '5 pts de [?] Y qui correspondent aux 5 pts de ramification' likely reads 'aux Y qui correspondent aux 5 pts de ramification pour M_{0,I}', i.e. the Y lying over the ramification points.
Last line is likely 'les Y' ∈ ... (3 élém.) en bijection avec les trois partitions de type 2,2 de I', continuing onto the next page.
'par le choix de SP_G, i.e. de [?]' is likely 'sur SP_G, i.e. ... par le choix de "pts bases" bien choisis'.
Under the J_II product, the underbraces read '0,1,…,2 facteurs' (number of loops) and '2 facteurs' (each wedge).
